thread:
alex: Heads-up — seeing gradual memory bleed on long streaming chats when tool loops are active. Not a hard OOM, more like a slow reservoir filling. KV resident set climbs steadily over hours.

maya: Can you repro locally or on staging? Any pattern on which tool calls trigger it?

alex: Repro on staging with a 12h long chat harness that cycles tools every ~30s. Snapshot after 2h vs 10h: KV live pages +24% and total RSS +18%.

sam: Pasted a mini profile from the staging run: 
```
kv_stats: pages_total=43200 pages_live=34821 pages_free=8380
page_splits=512 page_coalesces=7
slot_churn: allocs=1.2M frees=1.1M active_refs=92k
prefix_cache_hits=1.8M kv_gets=3.2M
```
Noticed `page_splits` is high relative to coalesces.

tara: @alex any change after the recent kernel-selector patch? We rolled 2.4.1 last week.

alex: We did roll kernel selection tweak for short-token kernels -> might affect allocation alignment. But the growth predates the rollout, it's slower. Still investigating whether allocation patterns changed and reduced page reuse.

maya: I ran flamegraphs of `kv_pagewalk` and `kv_free_sweep` — time in sweeps is stable, but amount of live pages keeps increasing. Suspect fragmentation + slow coalesce.

sam: Quick experiment: forced aggressive coalescing in the allocator on a forked build -> immediate drop in pages_live slope but CPU spikes and some tail latency regression. Paste diff: 
```diff
- coalesce_threshold=64
+ coalesce_threshold=16
```
That made fragmentation improve but introduced more background compaction work.

alex: Interesting. Could be two levers: (1) make coalesces cheaper or async, (2) reduce page-splitting heat by aligning small tool response writes into fewer slab spans.

kv-monitor-bot: [alert] kv_pages_live metric crossing 30k for run-id=stg-2026-03-16T02:45Z :page_with_palm:

maya: Repro note — the worst-case happens when tool loop appends many short deltas (~300B) to session context. Long chats that do a lot of append-only writes.

tara: Do we have per-tool write-size histogram? If small writes dominate, we can flip to coalescing buffer per-session and flush every N bytes/time. That reduces splits.

sam: I instrumented per-session write histogram. Top bin is 128-512B. Median ~240B. So yes, lots of tiny writes.

alex: Proposal: implement an in-memory append buffer for streaming sessions that groups small writes into 4KB flushes. Prototype locally shows 3x fewer page_splits and stable RSS over 8h. Need to test tail latency and failure modes.

maya: Can you push the prototype branch? I'll run the 12h harness overnight and collect heap profiles + page-level metrics. Also add a background async coalescer that yields to serving threads.

sam: FYI, rolling the coalescer sync -> async will need careful backpressure so we don't increase latency on p99. Might need to rate-limit compaction.

alex: Agreed. Plan: (1) append-buffer prototype PR, (2) async coalescer with token-bucket, (3) run staging 24h harness, (4) collect kv snapshots + perf counters.

tara: Sounds good. Tagging @eng-sre for capacity run scheduling. :thumbsup:

kv-monitor-bot: [note] scheduled run stg-longchat-2026-03-17 00:00Z (24h harness)

maya: Quick log snippet from the prototype run (after 10h): 
```
before: pages_live=34821 pages_splits/hr=58 rss=18.2GB
after:  pages_live=12210 pages_splits/hr=18 rss=12.6GB
```
Looks promising but need more runs.

sam: Keep an eye on p99 gen time — we saw a +15ms bump during async compaction spikes. Could be mitigated by smoother token-bucket.

alex: OK pushing PR for append-buffer now: https://git.internal/r/redwood/kv/compare/append-buffer-proto . Please review.

maya: Running overnight. Will share profiles in the morning. Thanks everyone.
